title: Flood watch in place on Vancouver Island as king tide impact continues
summary: A flood watch is in place for eastern Vancouver Island as the B.C. coast continues to deal with a series of storms that are combining with unusually high tides on Thursday.

image.caption: A person is seen near a rushing river in the Nanaimo area of Vancouver Island on Wednesday. A flood watch has been maintained for eastern Vancouver Island as king tides combine with a storm to continue to create hazards for coastal B.C. (Claire Palmer/CBC)

blocks.text: A flood watch is in place for eastern Vancouver Island as the B.C. coast continues to deal with a series of storms that are combining with unusually high tides on Thursday.
Swath of high streamflow advisories in place for the rest of Vancouver Island and the South Coast

The B.C. River Forecast Centre issued the flood watch on Wednesday, along with a swath of high streamflow advisories for the South Coast and the rest of Vancouver Island, as between 50 and 100 millimetres of rain were predicted to fall on the island.

Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) said in an orange coastal flooding warning for Metro Vancouver that "moderate to significant flooding" was expected along coastlines and low-lying areas due to storm surge and very high tides.

A number of evacuation alerts were issued by the regional districts of Nanaimo and Comox Valley on Wednesday, adding to previous alerts from the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation and Parksville, with residents told to be ready to leave at a moment's notice.
A warning to stay away from the river, posted by the Regional District of Nanaimo, is seen on Wednesday. (Claire Palmer/CBC)
The B.C. River Forecast Centre said in its flood watch that residents should stay clear of running rivers and never drive across flooded roads.

"Significant storms earlier in the month have contributed to saturated soils and higher flows, increasing the potential for rapid runoff and flow response during this next storm," the Wednesday flood watch reads.

blocks.text: The king tides currently hitting B.C.'s coast — referring to a phenomenon where cosmic alignments can mean dramatic tides which can be about 0.3 to 0.6 metres higher than the average — are expected to end on Thursday.
ECCC said the water levels could elevate by as much as 0.7 metres during high tide on Wednesday and Thursday.
While the coastal flooding warnings covered nearly the entire B.C. coastline on Wednesday, high winds and rainfall were also an issue for many areas.
B.C. Ferries cancelled a number of evening sailings between Metro Vancouver and Vancouver Island, citing high winds in the Strait of Georgia, on Wednesday.

The Metro Vancouver Regional District said that the Grouse Mountain Regional Park in North Vancouver — which houses the popular Grouse Grind trail — would be closed on Thursday due to the heavy rain in the forecast.

"Park staff will assess and determine if trails are safe to reopen once weather conditions allow. Please stay out of the park for your safety, that of park staff, and first responders," the regional district said on Wednesday.
